**Triage — R+118.** `bug` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:ui`. ⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched.

## Verification (`origin/main` `ac8d523`)

Confirmed. `packages/plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.ts:19` declares `export interface ObjectSchemaLike`, and it is the `childSchema` parameter type on **six** exported functions there (`:121`, `:208`, `:267`, `:314`, `:366`, `:429`). It is **not** re-exported from `packages/plugin-form/src/index.ts` — `git grep` for the name in that file returns nothing. So a consumer importing the package cannot name what those parameters require.

## ⭐ One fact the card does not have, and it changes the fix

There is a **second, unrelated `ObjectSchemaLike`** in the same package: `packages/plugin-form/src/schemaDefaults.ts:89`, declared `interface` with **no `export`**, used at `:200` and `:258`.

⇒ Two different types share one name inside one package, and only one of them is even module-exported. That makes the obvious one-line fix — re-export the name from `index.ts` — actively hazardous: whichever one is lifted, the package's public surface gains a name that already means something else a few files over, and a later reader has no way to tell which is which from the name alone.

⛔ I did **not** measure whether the two are structurally compatible. That is the first thing whoever takes this should do, because it decides the shape of the fix:

- **structurally identical** ⇒ deduplicate to one declaration, then export it;
- **structurally different** ⇒ ⛔ do not export under this name. Rename at least one at the point of declaration first, then export.

Stop-condition: report the structural comparison in the report either way. A PR that adds one `export` line to `index.ts` without stating which of the two it exported and why is not answering this card.

## Anchoring

`domain:ui` — `packages/plugin-form` is a published library, and under the objectui three-stream split published libraries and apps go to `domain:ui`. ⛔ Not `domain:spec`: the spec lane's objectui surface is `packages/types` and the schema corpus, and no contract in `packages/types` changes here.

## Why `p2`

Nothing is broken at runtime and no behaviour is wrong. But it is a **published package** whose exported functions cannot be called from TypeScript without re-declaring their parameter type by hand, and the duplicate name means the cheap fix can make the surface worse. Real, bounded, not urgent.

## Seat ruling on the surface question: **A** — export both, each renamed. And three of this card's own stated facts are false.

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. Delivered as draft PR **#7504** (`e3ea71f03`), Clause-② yes, `needs:contract-review` on both carriers, tier review commissioned.

### ⭐ The stop-condition was answered, and the answer turns on one token

The triage required the structural comparison before any export. Measured with `tsc` rather than read off:

> The two same-named declarations are **mutually assignable as written — but that is an artifact of `any` and nothing else.** Change the single token in `deriveMasterDetail`'s `Record` value type from `any` to `unknown`, leaving all else identical, and the child-to-defaults direction fails with **TS2322** while defaults-to-child keeps passing.

⇒ True relation: the `schemaDefaults` type is a **strict subtype**, not an equal, and the two differ in member set (the child one has `name`). **Structurally different** ⇒ per the stop-condition, ⛔ neither was exported under the shared name. Both were renamed at their declaration sites first — `ChildObjectSchemaLike` and `FieldDefaultsSchemaLike`.

⚠️ This is the finding that justifies the fence. A naive assignability check answers *"identical, go ahead and deduplicate"* — and would have merged two types that are not the same, under a name that already means two things. `any` makes almost anything assignable; **an assignability check over a type containing `any` is not a reading**.

The same rigour applied to option B, and it fails in the **opposite direction** from what the card and my brief both guessed: `ObjectSchemaMetadata` **narrows** rather than widens — it requires `name` (TS2322), requires a `type` on every field so the minimal fixture today's call sites pass stops compiling (TS2741), and has **no `reference_to` member at all** (TS2551) while `isCurrentUserSeedField` deliberately honours both spellings. ⇒ B is refused on evidence, not on preference.

### ⚠️ Three of this card's stated facts are false — verified by this seat, not taken from the report

| the card says | measured on `main` |
|:--|:--|
| "the parameter type of **three** exported functions" | **one.** `index.tsx:102` exports only `omitServerResolvedDefaults` and `isRequiredInForm`; a docblock at `:93-95` argues `schemaDefaultValues`, `seedCreateValues` and `SeedContext` are **deliberately** withheld |
| "`SeedContext` … **is** exported. `ObjectSchemaLike` is the one that is not" | **`SeedContext` is not exported either** — it is named in that same "deliberately NOT" list, and `git log -S` shows it never was on the entry |
| (triage) `git grep` in `index.ts` "returns nothing" | ⭐ the entry file is **`index.tsx`**. The negative was real but **arrived for the wrong reason** — the grep looked at a file that does not exist |

The card's central premise still holds — a published function's parameter type is unnameable — but its contrast ("the sibling type is exported, this one isn't") was the argument for urgency, and that contrast does not exist. Recording it so the next reader does not inherit it.

### The ruling

The implementer exported **both** types and routed the choice up rather than deciding it silently. Options as it framed them: **A** rename both and export both · **B** export only the card's one · **C** export one under the bare name `ObjectSchemaLike`.

**Ruled: A**, which is what landed. Reasoning:

- ⭐ **The card named the smaller instance.** `ChildObjectSchemaLike` is the `childSchema` of **five** entry exports; the card's own type is the parameter of **one**. B fixes the one and knowingly leaves the identical defect live on five published signatures — worse than before, because it would now be a defect someone looked at and stepped over.
- ⛔ **C is the worst option and the card's own subject explains why.** A maximally generic name whose actual shape is `name` plus a bag of `any` is the shape most likely to be adopted as a consumer's schema type in place of the shipped `ObjectSchemaMetadata` — publishing the collision instead of retiring it.
- **Scope discipline is respected in kind, not waived**: both additions are **type-only**, add zero runtime surface (pinned), and each is the type a signature *already published* requires. ⛔ Not an adjacent name lifted because it was nearby — which is exactly the class `index.tsx`'s own docblock refuses, and that refusal is why `SeedContext` stays off.

This is a **scope call**, which is the seat's. ⛔ It is not a ruling on the published surface's shape — the commissioned tier reviewer has been pointed at the both-vs-one decision explicitly and can reject it.

### ⭐ One test-design point worth keeping

The reverse verification includes a control that exports the **wrong one** of the two, and it fires. The implementer's note on why it had to be built the way it was:

> under that same mutation the README snippet and the consumer-held literal **still compile** — i.e. an assignability-based control would have waved it through.

So the controls are built on the two facts `any` does not erase: the member sets differ, and one field value is `any` where the other is pinned. ⇒ **When the thing under test contains `any`, a control that tests assignability tests nothing.**

### Filed, not folded in

**#7502** — `@object-ui/fields` has the identical defect with a **third**, structurally distinct `ObjectSchemaLike`: `deriveLookupColumns` is on the package root via `export *` while its `objectSchema` parameter type is unexported, and its sibling `DeriveColumnsOptions` **is** exported. Correctly kept out of this PR — a different package and a different shape, and folding it in would have made this card's surface decision harder to review.
